system.star: G1V, yellow-white, quiet, 3.8 Gyr old, 1.05 Lsun

facts.claim: Star: a quiet G1V, yellow-white, 1.05 L☉, 3.8 Gyr old; UV 1.15× the Sun's
facts.justification: The art fixes a yellow-white sun and a blue sky.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee; merged by opus

facts.claim: Gravity 1.05 g (R 1.04 R⊕, M 1.14 M⊕)
facts.justification: Slightly heavier than Earth: falls and cliffs matter; giants are allowed by oxygen, not by low gravity.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee; merged by opus

facts.claim: Day 26 h; twilight ~38 min (thick air scatters more), long dawns and dusks
facts.justification: see the claim

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee; merged by opus

facts.claim: Dense air: 1.6 bar
facts.justification: Sound speed stays ~345 m/s (it depends on temperature, not pressure), but low frequencies carry 1.6–2× farther on still, foggy dawns (temperature inversions duct them along the ground); high pitches die within tens of metres in fog and grass. Drag is 1.6× Earth's: terminal velocity ~25% lower, gliding cheap, sprinting costly.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee; merged by opus

facts.claim: Oxygen 21% → pO₂ ≈ 0.34 bar (1.6× Earth's)
facts.justification: Large aerobic bodies and costly organs (glow, sonar, spines) are affordable. Fuels stay wet, so lightning fires are rare: fire is a drought-year event.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee; merged by opus

facts.claim: One large moon: 1.2 Lunar masses at 450,000 km; month 29.7 d; spring tides every 14.9 d
facts.justification: Moonlit nights are bright; moonless nights are truly dark.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee; merged by opus

facts.claim: The island is a hotspot stratovolcano, 1.2 Myr old, ~2,050 m high, visible top 3.6 km across over an 8 km submarine base
facts.justification: Last eruption ~400 years ago: dormant, with fumaroles and hot springs.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee; merged by opus

facts.claim: Fog: cold upwelling sea on the west coast meets warm volcanic ground; the east start valley is a fog trap about 180 mornings a year
facts.justification: Evening convection storms on the 26 h day; lightning is frequent.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee; merged by opus

facts.claim: Rock: andesite makes steep, unstable cliffs; basalt makes lava tubes (the caves)
facts.justification: The sunken cave is a lava tube flooded by the sea; the hidden cave is a dry upper tube; the waterfall cave is an overhang in soft tuff.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee; merged by opus

facts.claim: Flares: C-class about monthly, X-class about once per 40 years (an old G dwarf is quiet)
facts.justification: A flare is a rare world event: auroras, UV pulses at altitude.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee; merged by opus

facts.claim: Orbit 1.02 AU; year 367 Earth days = 339 local days; axial tilt 26.5°, eccentricity 0.02: four seasons of ~85 local days, a bit stronger than Earth's
facts.justification: see the claim

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee; merged by opus

facts.claim: An inner sibling planet at 0.62 AU, a cloudy super-Earth: "the evening star". Being inside our orbit it is only seen near the setting or rising sun
facts.justification: (The faint line from the setting sun to it is the Petrova wink, A20.)

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee; merged by opus

facts.claim: Tides 0.4 m in open ocean but ~3.2 m on the island's shelf (shelf resonance, Bay of Fundy-style but milder): at spring low tide a causeway to the islet opens
facts.justification: see the claim

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee; merged by opus

facts.claim: Magnetic field 1.8× Earth's; surface UV 0.9× Earth's at sea level (more ozone in the thick air) but 1.4× at 2,000 m: the high slopes are a UV hazard
facts.justification: see the claim

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee; merged by opus

facts.claim: Composition N₂ ~77%, O₂ 21%, Ar 1.5%, CO₂ ~0.1%, humid
facts.justification: Mean sea-level temperature 14 °C; lapse 6.2 K/km; snow above ~1,750 m in winter and in shaded gullies all year.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee; merged by opus

facts.claim: Smell: molecular diffusion ~0.6× Earth's, so in still air scent trails last ~1.6× longer; in wind the advantage disappears
facts.justification: Scent is a dawn-and-fog sense.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee; merged by opus

facts.claim: Sky: deep blue zenith, milky horizon, copper sunsets (1.6× Rayleigh depth)
facts.justification: see the claim

facts.claim: Rain shadow: westerlies make the west coast wet and forested; the east meadows (the start valley) are drier in summer, with a spring
facts.justification: see the claim

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee; merged by opus

facts.claim: Wind force per m/s is 1.6× Earth's: gales in winter push light creatures and favour low, heavy bodies on exposed ridges
facts.justification: see the claim

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee; merged by opus

facts.claim: Seas: salinity ~3.8%, carcasses float and drift ashore; the shallows are turbid (visibility under 10 m) from volcanic sediment and plankton, so sea creatures rely on pressure sense, touch and electric sense more than sight
facts.justification: see the claim

facts.claim: The rock spire is a hard dyke left standing by erosion; the giant tree grows at the spring where that dyke dams groundwater
facts.justification: Sea arches and islets are dykes and drowned cones the sea has not yet cut.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee; merged by opus

facts.claim: Two arrivals
facts.justification: The FIRST seed capsule fell into this world's ocean ~900 million years ago and started all life (the cell stage). The meteor crater on the island is the SECOND arrival: 600 m wide, 25 m rim, ~12,000 years old, in cohesive tuff; a ~40 m iron-nickel body carrying a second, smaller capsule (the makers' follow-up). The 5 shards lie along one bent ejecta ray. What the second capsule did is the stage's mystery (it ends at the crater with cognition).

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee; merged by opus

facts.claim: Minerals creatures eat: salt from spray and seeps, calcium from shell beds and bone, basalt/olivine grit (gastroliths), kaolin clay (gut detox), sulfur at fumaroles
facts.justification: Poisons: arsenic and mercury in hot-spring crusts, SO₂ and H₂S near vents and in stagnant cave pools, copper in green crusts. Mineral licks are fixed points: migration corridors and ambush sites.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee; merged by opus

facts.claim: One biochemistry from the seed capsule: a porphyrin photosystem, DNA-like heredity, L-amino acids, a nitrogen-fixing symbiont
facts.justification: Any carcass can feed any creature, and parts can graft between lineages.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee; merged by opus

facts.claim: Plants are green by ancestry (the seed's pigment), not because green is optimal
facts.justification: Under strong UV (high slopes) and in poisonous plants they paint red-purple pigments over the green: leaf colour is an honest, readable signal of altitude stress and of alkaloids.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee; merged by opus

facts.claim: Food: sugars, starchy fruit, flesh, chitin, bone, salt
facts.justification: Poison: alkaloid plants (red-veined), H₂S pools, raw sulfur (poison to eat, fuel for the fire-breathing lineage).

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee; merged by opus

facts.claim: The island's life is an island radiation: the island rose 1.2 Myr ago (F7) and was colonised by a few founders that rafted, swam or flew from the mainland, then split into many species (like Hawaiian honeycreepers or Galápagos finches on Earth)
facts.justification: So cousins are recognisable, convergent solutions are everywhere, giants and dwarfs appear (island rules), and some niches are still empty (room for new species).
